Scene Foundation

Sky, atmosphere, terrain, lighting, shadows, grade — plus a time-of-day and weather system so one zone spans both reference art directions. The dependency root; every other system renders on top of this.

Passed bar iteration 2

Rubric sectionScoreRead
R1 Lighting & tonemapping 2.8 Sky scattering, IBL ambient and colour space all read PS4-tier. Held back by a flat white clipped patch around the sun disc in grazing and dawn.
R2 Shadows & contact 2.3 Contact darkening under rocks is convincing (3/4). Killed by R2.2 at 1/4 — a mechanically regular corduroy ripple raked across the midground in 7 of 9 shots.
R3 Terrain & world scale 2.2 Layered silhouettes and aerial perspective are genuine strengths (3/4 each). Ground detail at eye height scored 1/4 — the same ripple artifact.
R4 Foliage & density 1.6 Weakest section. Backlit translucency 1/4 (scrub reads as flat opaque silhouettes), wind 1/4 (no coherent gust direction), density countable rather than a field.
R5 Post & atmosphere 2.5 Per-weather grade praised as genuinely PS4-tier and clearly differentiated. Bloom bleeds into non-HDR sky around the sun.
R6 Time-of-day & weather 2.2 Night (3/4) and golden hour (3/4) are authored and hold up. Overcast nearly shapeless (1/4) and storm wetness reads as a colour shift, not water (1/4).

ROUND 2 LANDED. The corduroy ripple both critics independently traced to macRelief() is gone from every shot. Scatter density is up 3-4x inside the playable bowl, storm now shows real standing water, and backlit scrub genuinely glows gold against the dark hillside — the FFXV money shot works. Not re-scored yet.

Character System

Original humanoid mesh, skeleton, skinning, PBR materials, idle animation. No copyrighted likeness or ripped rig.

Passed bar iteration 3
not yet scored

Critic — biggest gap

OZ REBUILT — and the fix was architectural, not a bug hunt. The head was being polygonized by surface nets on a 5.8mm grid, but a stylized anime face is built from 1-2mm crisp edges: a lash line, a brow edge, a lip line. A fifth of a cell. No amount of re-seating primitives could ever resolve those features, which is why two rounds of repair kept producing speckle. The SDF head and hair meshing passes were removed entirely and replaced with an analytic head surface, with every feature authored in face-relative coordinates — across the face, above the eye line, along the normal — so a feature structurally cannot end up buried inside the skull. Features are now exact triangles: sclera lens with upper-lid cast shadow, iris with limbal ring and value gradient, pupil, two specular dots, a tapered lash line with an outer flick, brow ribbons. Hair is a lofted cap plus 23 sculpted bezier spikes. Sword and flute are on his person. 45,362 triangles, one draw call, and two back-to-back capture runs hash bit-identical.

Next action

Remaining: no cel shading or outline pass yet (the single biggest remaining lever for an anime read), hair has no secondary motion so it will feel stiff at a run, gaze is baked so he cannot look at anything, no visemes, and the sword under-reads at hero distance because the coat flare eats its upper half.

Environment, NPCs & Enemies

NPC and enemy characters reusing the player rig, plus props, landmarks and set dressing that make the basin a place rather than terrain.

Refining iteration 1
not yet scored

Critic — biggest gap

SNAGULAS BUILT — three types from one generator. Grunt at 1.66m squat and barrel-chested, stalker at 1.92m starved with long claws and a whip tail, brute at 2.10m with two metres of shoulder and 98mm tusks. Held constant so they read as a family: hunched carriage, forward-hanging arms, fixed snarl, recessed red eye under a heavy brow. Instanced skinning via a bone-palette texture keeps it to one colour and one shadow draw per species and LOD. Built on the same rig as Oz, with its three unused cloth bones re-seated as a tail so it gets lagged sway for free. Not yet wired into main.js.

Next action

Wire into main.js alongside combat and the boss, then playtest a real fight.

Player, Audio & UI

Third-person controller with terrain collision, adaptive synthesized score and ambience, and the HUD overlay. Everything audio is generated in code — no samples, no copyrighted music.

Passed bar iteration 2
not yet scored
no captures yet

Critic — biggest gap

Movement unblocked and verified by real playtest, not screenshot: pressed P, held W and moved 8.46m at 5.6 m/s matching RUN_SPEED, sprint at 8.27 m/s, 60fps flat. The bug was that character.js exposed the skinning skeletons root BONE as the world transform node, and the animator resets every unposed bone to rest each frame — so it snapped the character back to the origin immediately after the controller moved it. Audio, HUD and quest flow all verified earlier.

Next action

Player controller is the critical path — the animator overwrites the controller position writes each frame, so the character cannot move. Fixed first next round.

Every mesh, texture, and shader in Macrion is generated procedurally in Three.js — no asset packs, no downloaded textures. Frame captures are produced by tools/shots.mjs driving headless Chromium on the GPU, at fixed camera poses defined in docs/CAPTURE_CONTRACT.md, so every iteration is compared from identical viewpoints.

The visual bar is graded against reference frames from Final Fantasy XV and God of War, held locally and used for critique only. Those frames are copyrighted and are deliberately not reproduced on this page; the traits extracted from them are written up in docs/REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.md. The dark tick on each score track marks the 78/100 ship gate.
